title: The Musical Alphabet
body: Western music names pitches A–G, repeating each octave. The piano's white keys are naturals; black keys are sharps/flats (C♯ = D♭). An octave holds 12 pitches; a half step is the next key, a whole step two. No black keys sit between E–F or B–C.

title: Intervals
tagline: The atoms of melody and harmony
body: An interval is the distance between two notes: C→E is a major 3rd (4 semitones); C→G a perfect 5th (7). The tritone (6) is the restless 'devil's interval'. Chords are stacked intervals; scales are chains of them.

title: Scales: Major & Minor
tagline: W W H W W W H
body: The major scale runs W W H W W W H (C major = all white keys). Natural minor is the major from its 6th degree; C major and A minor are relatives. Harmonic minor raises the 7th for a stronger pull home.

title: The Modes
body: Each major scale hides seven modes: Ionian (major), Dorian (minor +♯6), Phrygian (minor +♭2), Lydian (major +♯4), Mixolydian (major +♭7), Aeolian (minor), Locrian (♭2♭5). One changed note changes everything.

title: Chords & Harmony
tagline: Stacked thirds and the pop loop
body: Triads stack two thirds: major (bright), minor (dark), diminished (tense), augmented (floating). Sevenths drive motion. The pop loop I–V–vi–IV and the dominant's pull to I are harmony's engine.

title: Circle of Fifths
body: Twelve keys a perfect 5th apart: clockwise adds sharps (F♯ C♯ G♯ D♯ A♯ E♯ B♯); backwards adds flats. Read signatures instantly; find relative minors; neighbours share six of seven notes.

title: Rhythm & Meter
body: Note values halve: whole, half, quarter, eighth. Simple meter divides beats by 2 (4/4); compound by 3 (6/8). Syncopation accents off-beats. Most world music is cyclical — tala and timelines loop.
